text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.8% today to $151.22, driven by a sharp spike in oil prices on geopolitical tensions. Brent crude hit $116—a six-month high—as the U.S. escalated rhetoric around Iran and reportedly readied military strikes, with diplomats being pulled from Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks on oil infrastructure. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly boost the value of the oil it produces and sells.

This move fits a broader energy rally over the past two weeks (COP up 12.77% since mid-October) as Middle East conflict risks have risen sharply. The combination of Ukraine's disruption to diesel supply and U.S.-Iran tensions has pushed crude toward levels not seen since spring, creating an environment where oil producers' profits expand—and their stock prices tend to follow.
